research14_dispositions.evidence: No calibrated DMG versus CGB-E analog high-pass-filter reference is admitted; the emulator filter remains a software policy.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a model-specific reference and an independent analog or hardware oracle.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG and CGB-CPU-E analog high-pass filter

research14_dispositions.evidence: The normal-speed CGB-E STAT ROM matches 5/14 source rows; a private one-dot twin changes the named row, but does not isolate one STAT-line event.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Promote only after a source-derived boundary, passing CGB-E guest assertion, and retained defect control.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB-CPU-E native CGB at normal speed

research14_dispositions.evidence: Post-boot PPU mode, LY and STAT literals differ by model; admitted cases do not select the CGB line-zero timing behavior.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with an independent post-boot timing discriminator for native CGB-E.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG and CGB post-boot PPU mode, LY and STAT

research14_dispositions.evidence: CGB VRAM lock-edge offsets remain unmeasured; no admitted case selects a different edge from the current fail-closed model.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a model-scoped VRAM access-edge oracle and adjacent passing boundary control.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB native-mode CPU VRAM access during mode 3

research14_dispositions.evidence: CGB OAM lock-edge offsets remain unmeasured; the inherited mode-3 cases do not isolate OAM access boundaries.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a model-scoped OAM access-edge oracle and adjacent passing boundary control.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB native-mode CPU OAM access during modes 2 and 3

research14_dispositions.evidence: CGB-E power-off state clear and Wave RAM retention are guest-tested; DMG length-counter retention has no executed case.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Keep UNKNOWN until an independent DMG length-retention fixture and explicit baseline revision exist.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB-CPU-E APU power state and DMG-CPU-B length retention

research14_dispositions.evidence: CGB SC fast-clock unused-bit readback has no admitted independent discriminator in this phase.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a CGB-E guest that separates stored SC bits from read masks.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB SC unused fast-clock bit readback

research14_dispositions.evidence: CGB APU register masks and NR52 channel-status bits are checked against authored register behavior and the frozen DMG model.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Reopen only if pinned independent register evidence contradicts the tested contract.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB-CPU-E APU read masks and NR52 status; frozen DMG baseline

research14_dispositions.model_gate: BOTH/basis="CGB current-byte alias; DMG alias remains scoped software policy"
research14_dispositions.evidence: Active Wave RAM current-byte reads and sample-buffer separation are checked for CGB; DMG alias remains labeled as software policy.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Reopen only if pinned CGB-E evidence contradicts the read alias or latch contract.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB-CPU-E active Wave RAM read alias; DMG software alias policy

research14_dispositions.evidence: STAT mode and coincidence bits at LCD transitions remain timing-ambiguous; current CGB-E snapshots do not isolate the transition edge.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a source-derived read at the transition and a neighboring edge control.
research14_dispositions.applicability: CGB STAT mode and coincidence reads at LCD transitions

research14_dispositions.evidence: TIMA overflow and reload timing are not isolated by the selected research14 evidence.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a CGB-E timer overflow/reload guest and exact independent callback rows.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG versus CGB TIMA overflow and reload timing

research14_dispositions.evidence: JOYP select writes and interrupt side effects retain no selected independent discriminator.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a guest that separates select-line transition, low-nibble read and IF edge.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG and CGB JOYP select writes and IF side effects

research14_dispositions.evidence: LCD on/off timing remains unresolved; LCDC bit-zero meaning is assigned to separate CGB-mode sibling gates.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit LCD start/stop timing with bounded LY/STAT transition observations.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG and CGB LCD on/off timing; CGB LCDC bit-zero siblings remain separate

research14_dispositions.evidence: The STAT-write spurious interrupt is DMG-specific and has no independent CGB-E discriminator.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit only with a model-applicable source that separates the DMG quirk from CGB behavior.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG STAT-write spurious interrupt behavior

research14_dispositions.evidence: TAC write glitch timing is not resolved by the selected speed-switch results.
research14_dispositions.revisit: Revisit with a CGB-E TAC write-edge guest and an independent timer-phase expectation.
research14_dispositions.applicability: DMG versus CGB TAC write glitch timing

research14_dispositions.evidence: Serial data/control behavior and internal timing remain outside the selected independent cases.
